title: Thymoma and myasthenia gravis: Masaoka staging, WHO histology and extended thymectomy
subject: ss-ctvs
refs: Sabiston Textbook of Surgery 22e Ch 110 (The Mediastinum: Thymoma and Myasthenia Gravis)

steps.say: Thymomas are the most common primary neoplasms of the anterior mediastinum. Approximately thirty to fifty percent of thymoma patients have generalized myasthenia gravis. Conversely, ten to fifteen percent of all patients with myasthenia gravis harbor an underlying thymic neoplasm.
steps.tx: Primary neoplasms of the anterior mediastinum are predominantly **thymic epithelial tumors**. A clinical hallmark is their striking autoimmune link: 30 to 50 percent of thymoma patients present with **myasthenia gravis**, while 10 to 15 percent of all myasthenic individuals harbor an underlying **thymoma**.

left.title: Thymoma Cohort
points: Most common anterior mediastinal mass in adults
30 to 50 percent manifest generalized myasthenia gravis
Additional autoimmune links: pure red cell aplasia, Good syndrome

right.title: Myasthenia Gravis Cohort
points: 60 to 70 percent demonstrate thymic follicular lymphoid hyperplasia
10 to 15 percent harbor true neoplastic thymoma

steps.say: Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder of neuromuscular transmission. Circulating autoantibodies target acetylcholine receptors at the motor endplate, triggering complement-mediated receptor destruction. Patients present with fluctuating muscle weakness, ptosis, and life-threatening respiratory failure.
steps.tx: Pathophysiology involves pathogenic IgG autoantibodies directed against the **acetylcholine receptor** at the neuromuscular junction. This antibody binding triggers complement-mediated **motor endplate destruction**, accelerating receptor internalization and degradation, which produces fluctuating **muscle weakness**, ocular ptosis, and fatigable diplopia exacerbated by exertion.

nodes.label: Complement activation and membrane attack complex formation
Degradation of neuromuscular junction folds causing flaccid weakness

steps.say: The World Health Organization classifies thymomas based on the morphology of epithelial cells and lymphocyte content. Types A and AB are predominantly spindle-shaped with low malignant potential. Type B comprises round epithelioid cells with increasing cytological atypia, while type C represents invasive thymic carcinoma.
steps.tx: The **WHO histological classification** divides thymic tumors into prognostic subtypes: Type A and AB exhibit spindle-cell morphology with benign trajectories, **Type B1 to B3** exhibit progressive epithelial dominance and cytological atypia, and **Type C thymic carcinoma** exhibits overt malignant invasion.

rows: Spindle or oval epithelial cells, rare lymphocytes
Medullary thymoma; exceptionally low recurrence risk
Mixed spindle cells and abundant reactive lymphocytes
Favorable prognosis; rarely shows capsular invasion
Resembles normal thymus cortex; low malignancy
Equal mix of plump dendritic cells and lymphocytes
Atypical thymoma; aggressive local invasive behavior
Overt cytological malignancy lacking thymus organoid signs
Thymic carcinoma; high nodal and distant metastatic rate

steps.say: The Masaoka-Koga staging system guides treatment based on local invasiveness. Stage one is defined by an intact capsule without microscopic invasion. Stage two involves microscopic capsular invasion or surrounding fatty tissue invasion. Stage three invades adjacent organs such as the pericardium, great vessels, or lungs.
steps.tx: Clinical management is guided by the **Masaoka-Koga staging** system: Stage I is completely encapsulated, **Masaoka Stage II** exhibits microscopic capsular or surrounding fat invasion, **Masaoka Stage III** invades neighboring organs such as the pericardium or innominate vein, and Stage IV exhibits pleural or distant metastases.

rows: Microscopic transcapsular invasion into adjacent fat
Macroscopic invasion into surrounding mediastinal fat
Macroscopic invasion into pericardium, great vessels, or lung
En bloc radical multivisceral resection + adjuvant RT
Separate pleural or pericardial metastatic implants

steps.say: Extended total thymectomy is the mandatory surgical standard of care. The surgeon resects the entire thymus gland from the lower thyroid poles down to the diaphragm, extending from phrenic nerve to phrenic nerve. Removing all cervical and mediastinal ectopic thymic tissue prevents persistent myasthenia.
steps.tx: The mandatory surgical benchmark is an **extended total thymectomy**, requiring complete en bloc resection of both upper cervical poles alongside all anterior mediastinal and pericardiophrenic fat extending strictly from **phrenic-to-phrenic dissection** to eliminate all microscopic **ectopic thymic rests**. Meticulous surgical clearance of all mediastinal adipose tissues dramatically reduces future recurrence and promotes sustained disease remission.

nodes.label: Full median sternotomy or robotic closed-port entry
Identification and continuous preservation of bilateral phrenic nerves
Bilateral superior cervical horn dissection from thyroid capsule
En bloc removal of all thymic parenchyma and pericardiophrenic fat pads

steps.say: The landmark MGTX randomized trial established the role of surgery in non-thymomatous myasthenia gravis. In patients with acetylcholine receptor antibodies, extended thymectomy significantly improved clinical weakness scores over three years. Surgery also permitted significant reductions in oral corticosteroid requirements.
steps.tx: The landmark **MGTX trial** provided definitive randomized evidence that in **non-thymomatous myasthenia**, extended thymectomy combined with medical therapy significantly improves quantitative myasthenia scores, achieves higher complete stable remission, and enables marked **prednisone reduction** compared to medication alone over a three-year period.

left.title: MGTX Trial: Thymectomy Arm
points: Significantly lower average quantitative myasthenia score (6.15 vs 8.99)
Lower daily average prednisone dose (44 mg vs 60 mg alternate-day)
Reduced requirement for hospitalizations and crisis therapies

right.title: MGTX Trial: Medical Therapy Alone
points: Higher persistent symptom burden across 3-year follow-up
Sustained high requirement for chronic immunosuppression
Higher cumulative incidence of steroid-induced toxicities

steps.say: Minimally invasive thymectomy has become the preferred approach for early-stage thymomas. Video-assisted and robotic-assisted techniques achieve complete R0 resection rates comparable to open sternotomy. Patients can have significantly less blood loss, less pain, and shorter hospital stays.
steps.tx: For Stage I and II tumors, **robotic thymectomy** achieves oncological **R0 resection** rates and neurological outcomes equivalent to open transsternal sternotomy. The enhanced 3D magnification permits radical dissection while delivering **equivalent remission** rates with minimal blood loss and reduced chest wall morbidity.

rows: Gold standard benchmark across all stages

steps.say: Adjuvant radiation therapy is indicated following surgery for invasive tumors. Mediastinal irradiation reduces local pleural and mediastinal recurrence in patients with Masaoka stage two with capsular invasion, or stage three tumors. Postoperative radiation optimizes long-term disease-free survival.
steps.tx: Postoperative **adjuvant radiotherapy** is indicated following resection for **Masaoka Stage II and III** tumors exhibiting transmural capsular invasion or positive microscopic margins. External beam radiation delivers 45 to 54 Gy, achieving marked **local recurrence reduction** across long-term follow-up without increasing cardiac toxicity.

nodes.label: Masaoka Stage I: observation only (no radiation)
Masaoka Stage II with extensive invasion or Stage III: adjuvant radiation
Maintain local relapse-free survival > 85% at 10 years
